jobs:
  tests:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      # SDK 10 builds both; SDK 8 builds neither.
      - name: Set up .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4

          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build Underworld.csproj

      # The test project is deliberately outside Underworld.sln, so name it.
      # These never load Godot, and the game-data tests return early when the
      # .SYS files are absent.

        # Only the font tests. The rest of the suite reads save fixtures from
        # ../UW2GOG, which is proprietary game data this runner has no licence to
        # carry, so 30 of its 177 tests fail here through no fault of the code. Making
        # those skip is worth doing and belongs on issue #60, where the maintainer
        # already offered to decide the CI layout; it is not this branch's to take.
        run: |
          dotnet test tests/Underworld.Save.Tests/Underworld.Save.Tests.csproj \
            --verbosity normal \
            --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SysFont|FullyQualifiedName~InstallationValidator|FullyQualifiedName~SceneFontWiring"

    name: Font render test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up .NET

          # Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0 with LatestMinor roll-forward, which does not cross
          # to 10. A 10 SDK builds it happily but Godot cannot host it, and the failure is
          # silent: CoreCLR never starts, so no test writes a line and the log holds only
          # shutdown noise. Both are needed here.
          dotnet-version: |
            9.0.x
            10.0.x

      - name: Install xvfb
        run: |
          # Mesa too: xvfb supplies an X display but no GPU, so the software GL driver
          # is what actually rasterises the render test.
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libgl1-mesa-dri libglx-mesa0

      - name: Fetch Godot 4.3 mono
        run: |
          curl -sL -o godot.zip \
            https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/4.3-stable/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux_x86_64.zip
          unzip -q godot.zip
          echo "GODOT=$PWD/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux_x86_64/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux.x86_64" >> $GITHUB_ENV

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
